feature: Built-in titles whose words visibly come in, on moving backgrounds
summary: Every built-in title's headline now takes most of a second to arrive and is seen moving: twelve different entrances (rise, blur, mask slide, swing, typewriter, depth fly-in, tracking, fall from large, flip, wipe, tilt), each over its own moving background except one deliberately bare name card.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Any recording open.

try.do: Open the Library's Comps shelf, search Kinetic Bold and choose Insert at Playhead on its tile.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Home, then Space, and watch the first second: each word slides up out of its own line, one after another.
Insert Keynote Clean the same way and play it: the words rise in one at a time out of their own blur, then the line under them.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Insert Light Leak and let it hold: letters close up from wide tracking over warm light drifting across.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Play to the end of any title: the headline visibly leaves over its last half second instead of blinking off.
Open queue/audits/2026-10-12-title-set-contact.png and compare the twelve at 0 to 800 ms; play any 2026-10-12-title-set-<name>.mp4.

evaluate: Watching any title from its first frame, can you see the headline arriving rather than already standing?
Do the twelve entrances feel different enough from each other that the set has real variety?
Is anything too slow to arrive for a short screen recording (Kinetic Bold with a long headline, Behind Glass)?
Do any backgrounds compete with the words: Keynote Clean's specks, Tech Terminal's grid, Light Leak's warmth?
Does Minimal Underline earn its place as the one bare name card?
rough: No mock draws the built-in title designs or their entrances; the reference is the brief in docs/design/video-titles-polish.md and the research list on the task.

Why it looked still before, reproduced on the renderer: no headline was on its first frame, but every one was fully in 300 to 400 ms later (half second ins on Ease out expo, which is nine tenths done a third of the way through, moving words 8 to 12 points), and the old contact sheet sampled its 'in' frame at 45% of the whole title's arrival, after the headline had finished.

The bar is now a test on the real renderer (TitleEntranceInkTests): under 10% of the headline's ink on the first frame, 20 to 80% half way through its in, never all there before 400 ms, and the same going off. All twelve pass.
Words come in on a plain Ease out rather than Ease out expo so the move is still visible half way through; the depth entrances keep their even curve.
Outs are keys, not a reversed reveal: words fade, rise, blur or shrink away over the last half second. A per-word out would need the reveal to run backwards, which it cannot yet.
Light Leak and the Glow's aurora were toned down after the first sheet: the aurora behind Gradient Glow now glows teal and blue, because in the words' own pink and violet it swallowed them.

Lighter second lines (subtitles, roles, the kicker) wear the soft shade the restyle already gives words over a moving look; the Pill Card is now fully opaque so its white name reads over white footage with no shade.
With the moving backgrounds switch turned off, only Minimal Underline is offered, since every other title now stands on a moving look. That switch is on at Next defaults.

Which backgrounds to keep overall is still decision title-text-visibly-comes-in-and-every-built-in-t-ten-moving-title-backgrounds-are; whether the set looks produced is decision title-text-visibly-comes-in-and-every-built-in-t-the-twelve-built-in-titles-now-v.

Perf (1080p, debug, suite alone): every title draws a frame in 2.2 to 12.6 ms median, Gradient Glow the slowest; under the whole suite's parallel load Editorial Serif, Gradient Glow and Stacked Stagger read 17 to 20 ms, as other render perf tests also do there (logged on find-out-why-the-whole-test-run-hangs-in-the-mac).
